title: Construction and local exactness of the full Cech sheaf complex
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module, and
$(U_i)_{i\in I}$ an open cover. For $p\geq0$ and $y:\{0,\ldots,p\}\to I$ put
$U_y=\bigcap_l U_{y(l)}$ and write $j_y:U_y\to X$. There exist an augmented complex
$\epsilon:\mathcal F[0]\to D^\bullet$ and identifications of the underlying module
presheaves of $D^p$ with $V\mapsto\prod_y\mathcal F(U_y\cap V)$, intertwining the
usual alternating face differentials. Under these identifications each coordinate
of the degree-zero augmentation is restriction $\mathcal F(V)\to\mathcal F(U_y\cap V)$.
Moreover $D^p\cong\prod_y j_{y,*}(\mathcal F|_{U_y})$ and $\epsilon$ is a
quasi-isomorphism. This is the full complex with repeated indices, without any
bounded-above assertion or any assertion about a morphism out of $X$.

proof.text: For an open W construct the module sheaf P(W) = j_W,* (F restricted to W). Restrictions on intersections give P(Z) -> P(W) for W contained in Z. Apply the usual Cech complex functor to this opposite-opens functor, and augment by restriction. Products of module sheaves are sheaves. On an open V the equality P(W)(V)=F(W intersection V) and the product universal properties give the stated term, differential and augmentation identifications, including the isomorphism with the products of open direct images.

On each cover member U_i, insertion of index i contracts the augmented full Cech complex. Pair the alternating face terms: all cancel except the identity term, giving dh+hd=id including the augmentation degree. Thus the augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism after restriction to every U_i. Homology sheaves vanish locally on a covering if and only if they vanish, so the augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism on X. For an empty cover X is empty and every module sheaf is zero; the same statement holds.
